title: Guided escalation decision graph and safe-revert helper for incident-bot
author: Maya Li
release_notes: Adds a decision-graph engine to guide on-call escalation and remediation choices.
Introduces a reversible 'safe-revert' helper UI and bot command that automates guarded rollbacks with auditable checkpoints.
description:
Context and motivation: On-call engineers repeatedly asked for a lightweight, auditable assistant that helps decide whether to escalate, mitigate, or rollback during noisy incidents. This PR adds a decision-graph engine to incident-bot that codifies common escalation paths and a safe-revert helper that standardizes reversible remediation (preflight checks, dry-run, checkpoint creation, and one-click revert). The goal is faster, safer incident resolution with fewer ad-hoc rollbacks and clearer post-incident traceability.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a modular decision-graph DSL and runtime, integrates the graph into /incident advise flow, implements a safe-revert helper with a small UI modal and bot commands (/revert-safely <change-id>), and wires telemetry for choices to SLO-toolkit so we can correlate escalations with error budgets. Also includes a small simulator in slo-toolkit to exercise paths for training and QA.

Operational notes and safety: The safe-revert helper defaults to dry-run on first execution for any change-id older than 24 hours and requires a second confirmation for production namespaces. All revert actions create an immutable checkpoint recorded in the incident artifact store and annotate the change in our change-tracker so downstream monitoring/rollbacks are visible. Reverts require the 'revert:execute' permission; auditors can query revert:history via incident-bot.

Telemetry and follow-ups: The PR emits the following events to be consumed by SLO-toolkit: decision.choice, decision.path_length, revert.attempt, revert.success, revert.rollback_time. We plan to create dashboards in the next sprint to measure decision-to-action latency and revert success rate (linked_linear: ENG-4382).

If revert is triggered and telemetry shows >20% failure rate in first 10 runs, auto-fallback to manual mode and raise SRE-oncall.

QA checklist (in-description checklist preserved as a single string): [x] unit tests added and passing [x] integration tests passing [x] security scan triaged [x] docs updated [x] UX smoke-tested in staging

This PR is intentionally scoped to decision guidance and safe reverts; it does not attempt to automate full remediation flows or replace runbooks. It provides structured guidance and reversible tooling to reduce cognitive load for on-call engineers.
